item.title: High-ranking provincial officials charged with corruption
item.description: Four public servants and a legal officer are facing serious criminal charges following a crackdown by the Independent Commission Against Corruption [ICAC] into alleged misuse of public funds and obstruction of justice in New Ireland, Jiwaka, and Port Moresby. Among those charged is New Ireland Provincial Administrator and former Finance and Planning chief executive officer Richard Andia, who faces
item.content:encoded:
Four public servants and a legal officer are facing serious criminal charges following a crackdown by the Independent Commission Against Corruption [ICAC] into alleged misuse of public funds and obstruction of justice in New Ireland, Jiwaka, and Port Moresby.

Among those charged is New Ireland Provincial Administrator and former Finance and Planning chief executive officer Richard Andia, who faces three corruption-related counts under Sections 91, 383, and 404 of the Criminal Code Act.

ICAC alleges Andia unlawfully facilitated and received a payment of K85,000 to himself under the pretext of hiring his personal vehicle to the New Ireland Provincial Administration.

In Jiwaka, three provincial finance and executive officers were arrested over allegations involving hundreds of thousands of kina.

Jiwaka provincial government executive officer Kupun Marang was charged with two counts of misappropriation under Section 383A of the Criminal Code Act 1974. He is accused of misappropriating K100,000 under an alleged asset recovery exercise, and facilitating a separate K280,812.43 payment to his private firm, Holy Bush Trading, purportedly for a fencing project.

Provincial financial manager Siwi Takai and finance officer/examiner Kelly Kumasan were also arrested and charged with misappropriation under Section 383A for their alleged role in approving the K280,812.43 payment to Holy Bush Trading.

All three Jiwaka officials have been granted bail. Marang is expected to appear at the Minj District Court on August 27, while Takai and Kumasan are set to appear on August 31.

Meanwhile, police in Minj arrested a man who allegedly tried to run over ICAC officers following a bail hearing at the local courthouse.

ICAC reported that Amban Ape drove his vehicle aggressively towards officers in an attempt to intimidate them, while shouting verbal threats demanding they stop investigations and leave the province. Police personnel on duty apprehended Ape, charging him with obstruction and threatening ICAC officers.

In a separate incident in the National Capital District, Securities Commission of PNG [SCPNG] legal officer Tonny Kawas was charged under Section 158 of the Organic Law on the ICAC for obstructing an investigator. Kawas is scheduled to stand trial at the Waigani District Court from October 5 to 7.

item.title: PNG’s youth bulge a ‘fact we must plan for’

item.content:encoded:
More than one in three Papua New Guineans are young people aged 15 to 34, putting immense pressure on schools, jobs, and health services across the country, according to new figures from the National Statistical Office [NSO].

Presenting at the World Population Day 2026 commemorations in Port Moresby today, NSO officer Shirley Kali revealed that PNG’s population has grown 3.4 times since 1980, rising from roughly three million to over 10.1 million in 2024.

However, the youth population is expanding at an even faster rate.

“36.3 per cent of this population is aged between 15 and 34,” Kali said.

“That is roughly one in three Papua New Guineans. Any policy or service that doesn't reach them is missing a third of this country.”

The 15 to 34 demographic has expanded 3.8 times since 1980, jumping from under one million to 3.7 million in 2024.

Demographers classify this rapid growth as a "youth bulge", a disproportionately large cohort entering their working and child-bearing years.

Kali emphasized that while this dynamic creates economic pressure, it also presents a major opportunity if managed correctly.

“It comes down to four areas: education and skills, jobs and livelihoods, health and reproductive health services, and evidence-based planning,” she said.

“This cohort is already here. It’s not a forecast. It’s a fact we must plan for.”

She said data from the 2024 National Population and Housing Census will be critical for tracking and managing this growth moving forward.

Ms. Kali urged the government, private sector, and local communities to invest heavily in education, healthcare, employment, and women's empowerment.

She said the choices young adults make over the next decade will define PNG’s socio-economic trajectory.

This year’s World Population Day was commemorated under the theme: “Choices, Lives and Futures: What shapes young adults' decisions about relationships, parenthood and the future.”

item.title: K1.2m land deposit paid for Manam resettlement
item.description: Displaced people of Manam Island in Madang will soon relocate to their new permanent home at Mumbndap in Bogia after a K1.2 million material deposit payment was handed over to traditional landowners last Friday. item.content:encoded:
Displaced people of Manam Island in Madang will soon relocate to their new permanent home at Mumbndap in Bogia after a K1.2 million material deposit payment was handed over to traditional landowners last Friday.

The Manam Resettlement Authority [MaRA] presented three Dyna trucks and four Lucas sawmills to the people of Mumbndap, as a breakthrough for more than 16,000 islanders living in care centres since the 2004 volcanic eruption.

The handover was witnessed by Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa, members of the Provincial Executive Council, and senior officers from the Department of Lands and Physical Planning and Department of Provincial and Local Level Government Affairs.

The 5,400-hectare Mumbndap site [formerly known as Andarum] is located 51.7km inland from Bogia station. One-third of the land lies within the Yawar local level government [LLG] in Bogia, while two-thirds sit in the Josephstaal LLG of Middle Ramu.

MaRA chief executive officer Richard Baia clarified that the vehicles and milling machinery were bought following direct requests from host landowners.

“They requested the trucks and sawmills because they now have a road and a vast forest area they want to mill,” Baia said.

The funds were drawn from a K10 million National Government allocation released in 2025, which included K4 million committed specifically for land acquisition.

Baia said the remaining balance of the K4 million is secured in a trust account managed by a board of trustees.

MaRA chairman Dr Boga Figa commended the resilience of the Manam people and acknowledged early champions of the project, including former judge Paul Akuram and former Madang governor Jim Kas, who pushed through the Manam Resettlement Act.

Land acquisition processes began in July 2013 with a Memorandum of Understanding between the provincial government and landowners. An access road has since been built up to the Renagam River at Sokmun village, with a bridge slated to cross into the main area.

“Manam islanders are now blessed with a second home where you can make gardens, plant coconut, betelnut, and sago without disturbance,” Dr Figa said, adding that residents retain the right to visit their original island home.

Dr Figa also acknowledged outgoing CEO Baia, whose three-year contract has ended, alongside community leaders Nelson Mambote and James Sukua.

Meanwhile, Department of Lands and Physical Planning customary land acquisition director Scott Gumahusa confirmed that while ground work is 90 to 95 per cent complete, the formal signing of the Deed of Release was deferred.

The 5,400ha parcel has been valued at K23 million.

“We cannot sign the Deed of Release yet because it is the legal proof of land sale to the State,” Gumahusa said.

“The deed is only executed when funds are exchanged for land, converting it to State land before issuing titles to authorities like MaRA.”

Representing 44 local host clans, MaRA board member Philip Bangtar thanked the National Government for advancing the long-delayed resettlement project.

item.title: Vanimo faces 3-month shortage as shipping crisis leaves shops empty
item.description: Shops across Vanimo have been running empty for almost three months, with basic household items like rice, tin fish, sugar, and coffee in short supply. The far northwestern town relies on cargo ships to bring in goods from Lae. But with only one shipping line now servicing the port, delays have hit businesses and families hard.
item.content:encoded:
Shops across Vanimo have been running empty for almost three months, with basic household items like rice, tin fish, sugar, and coffee in short supply.

The far northwestern town relies on cargo ships to bring in goods from Lae. But with only one shipping line now servicing the port, delays have hit businesses and families hard.

Consort Shipping Services and Bismark Maritime are the two main lines that operate to Vanimo Port.

According to the Sandaun Chamber of Commerce, Consort Express Lines suddenly stopped its service to Vanimo in early 2026.

That decision has left a backlog of cargo in Lae.

"Business houses have raised concerns over the backlogs of cargo in Lae that still needs to be shipped here to Vanimo," said Sandaun Chamber of Commerce President Gerald Gubon.

Consort Express was the primary domestic coastal shipper, connecting 15 to 17 ports across PNG, stopping its route to Vanimo has caused halts in businesses in Vanimo, Bismark Maritime is now the only shipping line shipping cargoes to Vanimo.

Chamber officials estimate there are 30 to 40 containers of goods still stuck in Lae waiting to be shipped.

During a tour of the new MV Karkar by Lutheran Shipping yesterday, business houses asked if Lutheran Shipping could assist by bringing in another cargo ship to clear the backlog.

The Chamber said it has already raised the issue with the Sandaun Provincial Government.

"We hope to find better ways to get a cargo ship in to ship all the backloads of cargo from Lae to Vanimo," Gubon said.

Residents and business owners are now calling on the government and shipping companies to restore regular services to avoid further shortages.

item.title: Gulf farmers complete cocoa pruning training
item.description: Nearly 30 local farmers, including a strong turnout of women and youth, have successfully completed a practical cocoa pruning training session in the Keipi Melaripi Local Level Government [LLG] area of Kerema, Gulf. The five-hour hands-on workshop, conducted on Tuesday by Cocoa Board Extension Field Officer Heni Smith, was a step forward for local growers following a years-long lapse in agricultur
item.content:encoded:
Nearly 30 local farmers, including a strong turnout of women and youth, have successfully completed a practical cocoa pruning training session in the Keipi Melaripi Local Level Government [LLG] area of Kerema, Gulf.

The five-hour hands-on workshop, conducted on Tuesday by Cocoa Board Extension Field Officer Heni Smith, was a step forward for local growers following a years-long lapse in agricultural extension services previously provided by the Department of Agriculture and Livestock.

During the session, participants applied their new skills directly in the field, successfully pruning 2,500 cocoa trees across a four-hectare development block, according to a statement from Lavare Cocoa officials.

Smith said each participant was equipped with a secateur [hand pruner], purchased and distributed by project leaders, to assist with proper maintenance techniques.

"The farmers were given hands-on instruction in proper pruning techniques for both old and young cocoa trees," Smith said. "This included removing unwanted growth to encourage healthy tree development and preparing the plantation for higher yield and productivity as the trees mature."

Smith added that the next phase of the program, focusing on broader cocoa block management, is scheduled to commence in October.

item.title: Elimbari TVET in Simbu gets new vehicle to drive students’ dreams
item.description: After two decades of service and nine years without a vehicle, Elimbari Technical Vocational Education and Training [TVET] in Chuave has finally received a brand-new Land Cruiser on Tuesday. For the last 9 years, the board, staff and students had no choice but to use PMVs to run school business in Simbu. Practical training and out-of-province student placements were also badly affected.
item.content:encoded:
After two decades of service and nine years without a vehicle, Elimbari Technical Vocational Education and Training [TVET] in Chuave has finally received a brand-new Land Cruiser on Tuesday.

For the last 9 years, the board, staff and students had no choice but to use PMVs to run school business in Simbu. Practical training and out-of-province student placements were also badly affected.

Headmistress, Sharon Aromo, said running a tertiary institution without transport has been extremely tough.

“It’s a big relief for the board, teachers and students,” she said.

The vehicle was officially presented today by Chief Executive Officer of the Chuave District Development Authority, Francis Aiwa, on behalf of the Chuave DDA and Chairman, James Nomane.

Speaking at the handover, Aiwa said the Chuave DDA, under the leadership of James Nomane, is prioritizing vital areas such as Education, Health, feeder roads, and infrastructure.

“TVET is a special institution where many of our youths can be trained to become skilled leaders in our communities,” he said.

He urged young people in Elimbari who are currently idle to register at Elimbari TVET for a better future.

Chairman of Elimbari TVET, Nimrod Koma, described the donation as a major boost and thanked the Chuave DDA for investing in the right place.

“Elimbari TVET continues to send students into Hospitality, Carpentry, and Mechanical trades,” he said.

Community leader, Paul Sinowai, spoke on behalf of the people of Elimbari and assured the DDA that the vehicle would be well taken care of.

Since the school’s establishment 20 years ago, only one vehicle had been provided by Simbu Governor Noah Kool during his first term. That vehicle was overused and eventually broke down.

The presentation was witnessed by the Chuave District Education Advisor, Chuave Police Station Commander Peter Lari, councilors of Wards 4, 5 and 6, of Elimbari LLG and members of the community.

item.title: Hela PHA warns of health risks amid El Niño drought
item.description: A public warning has been issued in the Hela province for people to take responsibility of their health and safety of their children as the province struggles with the severe El Nino weather conditions. Hela Provincial Health Authority CEO Dr James Kintwa said there are concerns of local water sources drying up and this could increase the risk of contamination.
item.content:encoded:
A public warning has been issued in the Hela province for people to take responsibility of their health and safety of their children as the province struggles with the severe El Nino weather conditions.

Hela Provincial Health Authority CEO Dr James Kintwa said there are concerns of local water sources drying up and this could increase the risk of contamination.

​"My appeal to the public is clear: any water fetched for drinking must be thoroughly boiled first," Dr Kintwa stated.

He also raised strong concern regarding street food vendors operating in Tari Town and along roadside stalls, warning consumers to exercise extreme caution, as due to financial pressures, some vendors might unknowingly or carelessly source water from contaminated supplies.

​​With waterborne illnesses expected to rise, Dr Kintwa warned that diarrhea cases are expected to surge unless the public avoids eating unhygienic, open-air cooked foods.

While acknowledging that street vendors rely on these sales to earn a living, he stressed that the current disaster makes it unsafe.

"Even if meals are prepared with clean water, selling food openly exposes it to heavy dust particles, posing a severe health hazard to both buyers and sellers".

Meantime, Dr Kintwa also announced that the provincial hospital will soon secure its own water supply. Specialized drilling equipment has arrived in the province to establish a borehole on the hospital site.

Dr Kintwa has thanked Hela Provincial Government and relief partners for their support, emphasizing that these crucial interventions will save lives as the drought persists.

item.title: SP appoints local talent as brewery manager
item.description: SP Brewery has appointed Noel Pepemik as the new manager for its Port Moresby Brewery, marking a major milestone in localizing senior operational leadership within the company. Pepemik earns the promotion following 14 years of dedicated service across various roles within the organization.
item.content:encoded:
SP Brewery has appointed Noel Pepemik as the new manager for its Port Moresby Brewery, marking a major milestone in localizing senior operational leadership within the company.

Pepemik earns the promotion following 14 years of dedicated service across various roles within the organization.

Hailing from Boikin in East Sepik, Pepemik overcame early personal hardship, losing his father at age 10, before completing his schooling with the support of his family. He attended Boikin Primary School and Brandi Secondary School before graduating from the Papua New Guinea University of Technology with a Bachelor of Science in Applied Chemistry.

After struggling to find employment as a fresh graduate, Pepemik joined SP Brewery in 2012 through its Graduate Development Program.

"It’s never easy finding your first job as a fresh graduate, and I was no different," Pepemik said. "SP Brewery gave me my first opportunity through its Graduate Development Program, and I remain grateful for that."

Over the past decade, Pepemik advanced through several key roles, including Brewing Supervisor, Brewing Manager in Lae [2020], Packaging Manager, and Acting Brewery Manager in Port Moresby [2025].

He attributed his progression to personal sacrifice, continuous learning, and strong mentorship from former senior industry figures, including the late Kuri Yuwai, Gia Vela, and Stella Ikasa.

"Many sacrifices were made along the way," Pepemik said. "I spent countless hours developing myself, often coming to work on weekends and days off to complete training and other development activities without expecting extra pay. That was my personal commitment to growth."

Pepemik emphasized that one of his most fulfilling achievements has been mentoring younger staff into leadership roles, noting that effective leadership involves preparing others to step up alongside you.

Encouraging young Papua New Guineans aspiring to build careers in the industry, Pepemik advised that commitment, discipline, and a drive for continuous self-development remain the key factors to professional success.

item.title: Joint US-PNG disaster exercise under way in Morobe
item.description: A four-day joint disaster management and humanitarian field training exercise between Papua New Guinea civil-military partners and international agencies is currently under way across Morobe to build local response capacity.

item.title: Simbu secures record STEM scholarship intake for studies abroad
item.description: 14 high-achieving Grade 12 students from Simbu Province have been selected to pursue overseas tertiary studies under the national Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics [STEM] scholarship program.
